alternatives_compared.name: repeat_control_rereads_after_bootstrap
alternatives_compared.approach: Reread lifecycle and optimizer state after the mandatory bootstrap before touching the semantic edge.
alternatives_compared.expected_time_to_root: worse; consumes the bounded semantic read budget without retiring an acceptance edge
alternatives_compared.quality: high control redundancy but low acceptance coupling

alternatives_compared.name: scheduler_snapshot_first_blocking
alternatives_compared.approach: Keep retrying the live scheduler surface until a current exact snapshot is readable.
alternatives_compared.expected_time_to_root: poor while the surface is unreadable and same-run polling/retry is forbidden
alternatives_compared.quality: strong physical certainty if readable but can starve semantic closure

alternatives_compared.name: bootstrap_once_then_spend_semantic_read_budget_on_first_unsatisfied_root_edge
alternatives_compared.approach: Treat the mandatory twelve-file bootstrap as the authoritative control read for the invocation; do not reread those same controls post-bootstrap absent an authority/CAS mismatch. Allocate post-bootstrap repository reads first to the C32 target-index/candidate consumer edge and second only to the exact candidate tuple or consumer trace needed to decide that same edge. Keep the single live scheduler attempt nonblocking and mutate nothing when its result is unusable.
alternatives_compared.expected_time_to_root: lower; converts bounded reads from duplicated control confirmation into acceptance-edge evidence while preserving authority and fail-closed scheduler behavior
alternatives_compared.quality: higher acceptance coupling and falsifiability without weakening CLEAN, provenance, scheduler, cost or protected-primary gates
